papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Smart Meter Energy Forecasting in Intelligent Power Grids
A machine learning framework for privacy-preserving financial risk assessment using explainable artificial intelligence and blockchain-based trust management
papers.abstract: Introduction Financial risk assessment requires models that jointly satisfy privacy, explainability, and decentralized trust, yet existing machine-learning approaches usually address these requirements in isolation. Methods This paper proposes the Privacy-Preserving Explainable Trust Framework (PP-ETF), integrating federated learning with differential privacy, post hoc SHAP and LIME explanations, and a permissioned distributed ledger for trust management. PP-ETF is evaluated on the German Credit and HELOC datasets against statistical models, centralized ensembles and deep networks, and privacy-preserving baselines. Results PP-ETF outperforms privacy-preserving baselines in AUC-ROC while remaining within 1.4%–1.6% of centralized deep-learning models. Reputation-based adversarial detection excludes a malicious participant within two communication rounds with a 3.2% false-positive rate. Explanation stability yields average cosine similarity of at least 0.87, and the ledger processes up to 480 transactions per second with 2.4 s finality latency. Discussion The results support the feasibility of jointly implementing privacy, interpretability, and decentralized trust under the evaluated conditions; they do not imply that the underlying trade-offs are eliminated. PP-ETF provides an end-to-end blueprint for effective, scalable, private, interpretable, and trustworthy risk-management systems.
papers.venue: Frontiers in Blockchain

papers.title: Observability Aware Federation Learning in Fog-IoT Systems Round Time and runtime Metrics Analysis through iFogSim-Based implementation
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables the training of models on distributed Internet of Things (IoT) and localization of them. Practically, Fog-IoT system More infrastructure differences exist in infrastructure, including differences in communication lag times, differences in access to fog resources, and differences in client activity that introduce much uncertainty in their effects on the length of the federation rounds, and the available literature is more focused on the effect of infrastructure dynamics on the execution of learning behavior than on how to optimally execute the federation process itself. This research aims to design an observability-enabled federated learning framework used to examine how varying conditions in heterogeneous Fog-IoT infrastructure affect the performance of federated learning. The proposed framework incorporates TensorFlow-enabled federated learning with the iFogSim2-based Fog-IoT simulation in order to capture heterogeneous devices, variability in communication, constraints in fog resources, as well as passive telemetry from training, systems, and behavioral layers. Experiments shown that communication latency and constrained fog resources greatly affect the execution of federated learning, since the time needed to complete each round is increased from 4.2-5.3 s in baseline conditions to 6.1-8.8 s in high latency conditions and 5.3-7.9 s in constrained fog resources. In addition, increased utilization of fog resources from 30% to 90% causes the ratio of stragglers to increase from 0.08 to 0.38. This set of findings proves that the heterogeneity of infrastructure is among the major predictors of FL performance and shows the viability of calculating observability to Fog-IoT implementation.
papers.venue: International Journal of Innovation and Technology Management

papers.title: IoTSplit: Teacher-Guided Federated IoT Intrusion Detection Using Small Language Models
papers.abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) networks produce large volumes of traffic, yet only a small portion may have reliable labels for training an intrusion detector. These labeled examples are distributed across locations that may observe different types of attacks. Federated Learning (FL) allows these locations to learn jointly, while a server teacher can provide predictions to help clients use their unlabeled traffic. However, transmitting every unlabeled flow to the teacher incurs substantial communication overhead. To address this issue, we introduce IoTSplit, a federated intrusion detection framework that consists of: (1) a fixed TinyLlama-based encoder that transforms local flow representations into compact numerical messages, reducing the amount of data transmitted to a server-side teacher; (2) a query-based training strategy that selects unlabeled flows within a query budget and uses the teacher's class probabilities together with available labels to train local detectors; and (3) a coordinator that aggregates local detector updates into a global model, enabling clients to classify new traffic locally without further interaction with the teacher. To evaluate IoTSplit, we conducted experiments using CICIoMT2024 dataset. The experimental results show that compact messages substantially reduce the amount of data transmitted to the teacher. Moreover, randomly selected flows receive more accurate teacher predictions than uncertainty-selected flows, highlighting the importance of teacher reliability when selecting flows for querying.
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series

papers.title: IoT, Edge, and Cloud Computing in Smart Cities
papers.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, and cloud computing are essential drivers of the smart city concept, enabling urban-scale sensing, immediate decision-making, and data-driven services. Their combined deployment is increasingly impacting city-wide cyber–physical systems, demanding the seamless operation of a variety of devices, networks, and computing infrastructures, frequently under demanding constraints of latency, reliability, privacy, and security. This Special Issue emphasizes the integration and mutual enhancement of these technologies within contemporary urban settings, underscoring both fundamental advancements and practical applications. This collection, aligned with Future Internet’s “Network Virtualization and Edge/Fog Computing” Section, encompasses topics such as cybersecurity, edge-to-cloud integration, data analytics, intelligent transportation systems, federated learning, cyber–physical systems, and sustainable urban development. The published contributions incorporate all aspects of the field, from resource management and distributed intelligence at the peripheral level, to secure and privacy-preserving mobility services, to computer-vision-based monitoring of urban infrastructure, while also providing wider architectural insights through survey and review studies.
papers.venue: MDPI eBooks

papers.title: Multi-Model Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Transceiver Beamforming and Device Grouping
papers.abstract: This paper considers uplink communication design for training multiple independent machine learning models via wireless federated learning. To reduce communication delay, we utilize multi-antenna beamforming and propose a multi-model over-the-air (M-OTA) uplink transmission and aggregation method for simultaneous training of multiple models. Devices are formed into groups for local model training based on the model assignments per communication round and simultaneously perform OTA aggregation over a multi-access channel. Based on the M-OTA transmission and reception process, we formulate a joint optimization of transmit and receive beamforming and device grouping over $T$ communication rounds to maximize the training convergence rates of all models. We analyze the per-model optimality gap, which captures the impact of noisy aggregation and inter-model interference on the learning performance. We further show that the $T$-round joint optimization problem can be decomposed into per-round online optimization to devise solutions. Following this, we propose a device grouping strategy that explores channel correlation among devices to maximize OTA aggregation performance. Furthermore, we present a low-complexity iterative algorithm for joint transmit-receive beamforming with closed-form updates. Simulation shows that our proposed M-OTA approach substantially outperforms the conventional single-model sequential OTA approach and other commonly used beamforming schemes.

papers.title: Federated training performs as well as centralized for 3D Latent Diffusion for Diagnosis-Conditioned Brain MRI Synthesis
papers.abstract: Generative models of brain MRI are useful to understand brain conditions, and to enrich scarce and imbalanced neuroimaging data. However, training these models requires large, multi-site training sets, which is challenging. Federated learning (FL) allows for training deep learning models without sharing data. We show that training a 3D conditional latent model federatedly (where data is kept private at each site) performs similarly to centralized training (where all the data have been copied to a single site). We evaluate three metrics: conditional fidelity (how well generated MRIs perform in classification), diversity (how the generated images match the real data distribution, using MultiScale-SSIM), and realism (how close generated images are to real images, using Fréchet Inception Distance). Our results show that federated training is a viable route to develop multi-site generative models of brain MRI.

papers.title: Compressed Per-Player Local Methods for Multiplayer Federated Learning: Exact Convergence via Increment Sharing
papers.abstract: Multiplayer Federated Learning (MpFL), introduced by Yoon et al. (2025), extends classical federated learning to settings where clients are rational players in a game with individual objectives and strategies, seeking an equilibrium. A natural baseline is Per-Player Local SGD (PEARL-SGD), where each player performs several local SGD steps before exchanging strategies through a central server. However, the original PEARL-SGD formulation does not extend cleanly to compressed communication. Directly compressing the players' strategies can prevent convergence to the equilibrium, even with deterministic gradients. To address this issue, we reformulate PEARL-SGD so that players communicate local strategy increments rather than the strategies themselves. Without compression, the two formulations are equivalent, but with compression, increment sharing preserves exact convergence, allowing us to design the communication-efficient compressed PEARL-SGD (C-PEARL-SGD). Beyond compression, we also consider variance reduction as another axis of improvement, introducing PEARL-SVRG and its compressed variant C-PEARL-SVRG. Under the original MpFL assumptions, we establish convergence guarantees for all variants through a unified parametric inequality. Numerical experiments, including distributed spectrum sensing, demonstrate the practical benefits of our methods over vanilla PEARL-SGD.

papers.title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning servers combine client models with a fixed aggregation rule, and each rule in common use is designed for one kind of heterogeneity. We study whether a large language model (LLM) that inspects the client models can choose the rule itself, without any training on the server. In FedReason, the LLM is called every ten rounds. It analyses the weights by running code in a restricted server-side sandbox, sees only the printed results, may score a few candidates on a 500-image proxy set, and submits a short Python aggregation program. The server applies the program until the next call and falls back to FedAvg whenever its output is invalid. Full weight tensors never leave the server. We evaluated FedReason with Claude Opus 5.5 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18 under Dirichlet label skew, width-heterogeneous sub-models and Byzantine clients, in 168 runs against 14 baselines. Across 12 paired label-skew runs it beat FedAvg by 1.26 percentage points on average (10 wins), and a control that spends the same per-round proxy budget on choosing among standard rules by 1.08 points. It was the strongest server-side rule on CIFAR-100 but did not beat SCAFFOLD, which changes client training. With three of ten clients malicious, it excluded all sign-flipping clients from the first round and stayed about one point below FLTrust without training a root model. Without proxy feedback, accuracy fell from 73.8% to 38.8% in one seed. A 60-round run cost 0.79 USD in API fees on average.

papers.title: GTAFL: Addressing Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning in Medical Image
papers.abstract: In healthcare, protecting patient privacy is crucial due to the sensitivity of medical data and its extensive accessibility. Federated Learning (FL) offers a decentralized and privacy-preserving training paradigm, making it an ideal solution for healthcare applications. A critical challenge in healthcare is that real-world medical data often exhibits long-tailed distributions in local and global views. Existing methods addressing long-tailed FL problem typically assume that the model will be evaluated on uniform test data distribution. However, practical test data in healthcare systems is often agnostic and unpredictable, leading to potential model failures in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we introduce a novel task termed Test-Agnostic Long-Tailed Federated Learning and propose GTAFL, a comprehensive framework to address this challenge. During the training stage, GTAFL employs adaptive re-sampling, expert classifier retraining, and self-supervised learning to correct biased classifiers and distorted feature spaces caused by long-tailed training distributions. During the inference stage, an ensemble mechanism combines retrained expert classifiers to handle test data with unknown distributions. Extensive experiments on CIFAR10 and two medical datasets manifest that our framework outperforms other state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/cgy-lavine/GTAFL

papers.title: Research Progress in Machine-Learning-Based Fault Diagnosis for Mechanical Equipment
papers.abstract: Fault diagnosis of mechanical equipment is essential for ensuring safe and reliable operation and reducing losses caused by unplanned downtime. With the large-scale deployment of sensors and the Industrial Internet of Things, condition-monitoring data have grown rapidly in both volume and dimensionality. Conventional diagnostic approaches that rely on human expertise and signal processing are increasingly inadequate, while machine learning, especially deep learning, has become the dominant research paradigm because of its automatic feature extraction and powerful nonlinear modeling capabilities. Following a data-feature-model-application framework, this paper systematically reviews advances in machine-learning applications for mechanical equipment fault diagnosis. It first outlines the basic diagnostic workflow, commonly used monitoring signals, and representative public datasets. It then reviews diagnostic methods based on conventional machine learning, including feature engineering, support vector machines, and ensemble learning, as well as deep-learning methods based on convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, autoencoders, attention mechanisms, and Transformers, comparing their principles, applicable conditions, strengths, and limitations. For real industrial environments, the paper focuses on emerging directions such as few-shot learning, transfer learning, multisensor fusion and graph neural networks, federated learning, and generative-adversarial-network-based data augmentation, and summarizes their applications to representative systems including rotating machinery, motors, computer numerical control machine tools, and pumps. Finally, current challenges are analyzed from the perspectives of data quality, model generalization, interpretability, and real-time edge deployment, and future trends involving physics-data integration, foundation models, and intelligent operation and maintenance are discussed. The analysis shows that the field is evolving from discriminative diagnosis dependent on large amounts of labeled data toward few-shot, cross-condition, interpretable, and deployable solutions. Data governance and engineering implementation will therefore become the principal bottlenecks constraining practical adoption.
papers.venue: Computers and artificial intelligence.

papers.title: Intelligent Intrusion Detection Systems Using Machine Learning Techniques
papers.abstract: The advent of intelligent intrusion detection systems (IIDSs) powered by machine learning and deep learning is revolutionizing the field of cybersecurity as they facilitate data-driven threat detection that extends beyond the limits of signature-based solutions. This chapter provides an in-depth review of contemporary intelligent intrusion detection frameworks, addressing aspects ranging from detection strategies, monitoring architectures to benchmark data sets and performance evaluations. The focus is on supervised learning, unsupervised learning, semi-supervised learning, and reinforcement learning approaches, encompassing ensemble learning, deep neural network-based solutions, graph neural network-based approaches, transformer-based methods, and combined CNN-RNN techniques. Other important factors considered in this study include adversarial robustness, privacy-aware and federated detection schemes, interpretability in AI, class imbalance problem, concept drift phenomenon, and encrypted traffic detection.
papers.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series

papers.title: ICUBE5: A Conceptual Multidimensional Benchmarking Framework for AI-Native Secure 6G Edge Architectures
papers.abstract: The trend towards sixth-generation (6G) networks requires a new network architecture capable of incorporating artificial intelligence (AI), distributed edge intelligence, security, governance, adaptability, and sustainability into increasingly heterogeneous computing and communication environments. Present methods to achieve such network architectures address only the optimisation, security, governance, or energy-efficiency issues separately, making it difficult to assess the maturity of a particular architecture across all of these dimensions. This paper proposes an AI-native secure edge architecture and introduces ICUBE5, a conceptual multidimensional benchmarking framework for assessing AI-enabled 6G edge architectures across five dimensions: AI Maturity, Security Resilience, Governance Alignment, Adaptive Stability, and Sustainability Efficiency. The framework provides a structured approach for normalising dimension-specific indicators and combining them through configurable weighting schemes that can be adapted to deployment priorities. Illustrative weighting scenarios are presented for general-purpose, industrial automation, smart-city, and energy-constrained edge environments to demonstrate how contextual priorities can influence the composite ICUBE5 score. A comparative analytical illustration involving cloud-centric, edge-centric, and AI-native secure edge architectural archetypes further demonstrates the application of the framework. Under the illustrative assumptions used in the analysis, the proposed AI-native secure edge architecture produces the highest composite ICUBE5 score, while the results remain conceptual rather than empirical measurements of deployed systems. The framework also incorporates security and governance considerations associated with adversarial machine learning, federated learning, trustworthy AI, and emerging regulatory requirements. ICUBE5 is therefore positioned as a benchmarking construct rather than a validated performance index. Future research will validate the framework through simulation and experimental testbeds, using measurable network, security, governance, adaptive-control, and energy-efficiency indicators. The proposed framework provides a basis for structured comparison and context-sensitive evaluation of emerging AI-native 6G edge architectures.
papers.venue: International Journal of AI and Advanced Computing

papers.title: FedTaste: Topology-Aware Structural Transfer for Multimodal Federated Learning with Missing Modalities
papers.abstract: Multimodal Federated Learning (MFL) faces client-level modality missingness and Non-IID data distributions, which can induce substantial representation drift and hinder effective cross-client collaboration. Existing approaches commonly rely on generative imputation, external auxiliary data, or isolated unimodal training to bridge modality gaps, often introducing additional computational, communication, or privacy concerns. We propose FedTaste, a parameter-efficient framework for topology-aware structural transfer in MFL with missing modalities. Rather than relying solely on first-order alignment, FedTaste exploits transferable group-level semantic relations within a shared semantic-group space. Full-modality clients use frozen vision-language encoders with trainable Modality-Adaptive Structural Prompts to distill joint relational structure, which the server consolidates into a confidence-aware global blueprint. Missing-modality clients optimize only the prompts attached to their available branches and align their partial representations with the blueprint through topology and spectral regularization. FedTaste therefore avoids explicit modality imputation and raw-data exchange during federated optimization while preserving shared semantic structure across clients. Experiments on standard cross-modal retrieval benchmarks show that FedTaste consistently outperforms representative baselines under challenging Non-IID and modality-heterogeneous settings while maintaining favorable communication efficiency.

papers.title: Machine Learning Meets Blockchain: A Domain-Oriented Review of Integration Mechanisms, Applications and Open Challenges
papers.abstract: Blockchain and machine learning (ML) are combined in systems that must learn from multi-party data and keep a verifiable record of what was used and decided. This scoping-style review of a ranked sample covers seven domains: healthcare, finance, supply chain, energy, smart contracts, transportation and education. We searched Scopus and IEEE Xplore on 15 October 2026, ranked 5195 candidate records, read 345 abstracts in rank order, coded a core corpus of 192 studies and read 38 in full. Federated learning is the most common method (93 of 192 core studies name it), and detection of fraud, intrusions and vulnerabilities is the most common task among the 38. None of the 38 reports a deployment, 24 report a measured ledger figure and two measure ledger energy. Ten use more than one privacy mechanism, and only two report accuracy with and without it. Attack tests are small, and one study tests a Sybil attacker. Studies differ too much to compare, so we do not rank domains. A ledger shows that a record has not changed, not that it was correct when written. The main gaps are realistic evaluation, shared benchmarks and reporting standards, and tested explanations for decisions made inside contracts.

papers.title: Data privacy and audit compliance of supply chain finance warehouse receipt pledge based on WSN federated edge learning
papers.abstract: Abstract In supply chain finance warehouse receipt pledge financing, the status of the pledged assets is difficult to verify in real time, the risk of privacy leakage of financing data is high, and the federal training process lacks verifiable audit trajectories for regulatory authorities. To achieve multi-warehouse collaborative risk control modeling under the condition of data not leaving the domain and meet the requirements of privacy protection and audit compliance, a method for privacy and audit compliance of supply chain finance warehouse receipt pledge data based on federated edge learning of wireless sensor networks is constructed. A pledge perception and digital warehouse receipt generation mechanism based on wireless sensor networks is designed. A federated edge learning architecture integrating trust and energy-aware weighted aggregation, federated proximal terms and communication compression is constructed. The study introduces a joint security aggregation mechanism of differential privacy and homomorphic encryption, as well as an audit compliance framework for blockchain smart contracts. The experimental results show that when the data heterogeneity parameter is 0.1, the test accuracy of the proposed method reaches 88.4%, which is 9.9% higher than the 78.5% of the federal average algorithm. In the ablation experiment, the F1 score of the complete method is 93.6%, while it drops to 88.9% after removing the federal proximal term. When the privacy budget is 0.10, the accuracy rate of the proposed method is 92.1%, which is 8.0% higher than the 84.1% of the federal average algorithm. The results show that the proposed method has stronger robustness under extreme non-independent homogeneous distribution conditions. Trust and energy-aware selection and federated proximal terms contribute significantly to accuracy, and the privacy enhancement mechanism achieves effective privacy protection with limited accuracy loss. This research provides a technical path that takes into account data privacy, model performance and audit compliance for the warehouse receipt pledge scenario in supply chain finance, which is conducive to promoting the compliant application of federated learning in supply chain finance risk control.

papers.title: Federated Learning: Foundations and ApplicationsRajkumarBuyya, AnweshaMukherjee, and Sajal K.DasMorgan Kaufmann/Elsevier, 2026, 366 pages, $200, hardcover ISBN: 978‐0‐443‐44433‐3
papers.abstract: Overview and ScopeFederated learning (FL) has emerged as an important approach to collaborative data analysis in settings where data cannot readily be pooled in a central repository.By allowing multiple institutions or devices to contribute to model development while retaining their local data, FL offers potential benefits for privacy, data governance and large-scale machine learning.However, it also introduces statistical and computational challenges, including heterogeneous data distributions, communication constraints, privacy-related information loss and difficulties in evaluating the resulting models.

papers.title: Accountable Verifiable Secure Aggregation with Dynamic Exit Tolerance for Vehicular Federated Learning
papers.abstract: In vehicular federated learning (FL), an edge aggregator may tamper with theaggregate, evict vehicles as dropouts, or repudiate rounds. Two failure modesarise: structural, where verification breaks once participants leave, and evidential,where malicious eviction is indistinguishable from genuine dropout. We presentAVSA, an accountable verifiable secure aggregation protocol with dynamic exittolerance. AVSA unwinds departed clients’ masks via threshold reconstructionof Shamir-shared ephemeral Diffie–Hellman keys, proves the aggregate with aconstant-size proof core verified asynchronously by a cloud coordinator, andbinds each exit to a signed, adjudicable declaration. In the random-oracle model,tampering or undeclared eviction is detected and located except with negligibleprobability. Evaluated on real BLS12-381 pairing operations and highD traces,AVSA verifies within seconds, reproduces the plaintext sum in 519 of 520 exit-tolerance rounds, and fits a 30 s round budget at N ≤ 100 on the high-bandwidthtier; larger cohorts exceed the budget.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Cyber Threat Detection for Modern Organizations: A Systematic Review of Challenges and Solutions
papers.abstract: The ability to adapt to threats using AI and ML techniques has become a major factor in the fight against cyber threats, offering a data-driven, adaptive approach to threat detection that transcends signature-based methods. With the growing surge of research and development on AI/ML-based intrusion detection, however, there has been disarray in the perception of the challenges which organizations are facing and the solutions available to them to tackle the challenges. This paper is based on a systematic literature review (SLR) carried out following the Kitchenham SLR protocol and a PICOC search strategy, and the analysis of 45 peer-reviewed and industry-reported studies related to the application of AI/ML for cyber threat detection. In total, the corpus identified 271 different challenges and 252 solutions, which were grouped into seventeen recurring categories of challenges. The biggest challenges to successful adoption were zero day and novel attack detection (36), scalability and big data (34), high false positive/negative rates (33), computational and resource constraints (32), and dataset imbalance (31), followed by outdated datasets, privacy and regulatory compliance, explainability, and high dimensional feature spaces. The comparison on the continental level also identified the scalability and IoT-based detection as the main challenge in Asia, privacy and explainability as the primary challenge in Europe, adversarial robustness and enterprise security as the main challenge in North America and foundational infrastructure and capacity limitations as the main challenge in the Middle East/Africa. The findings indicate a trajectory towards more hybrid, adaptive, and privacy-conscious approaches to AI security that integrate ensemble and deep learning techniques, federated learning, explainable AI, and ongoing training pipelines. This research work highlights the severity of challenges faced by the future organisations in implementation of AI/ML for cybersecurity intrusion detection.
papers.venue: Journal of Emerging and Innovative Technologies

papers.title: Performance evaluation of fault detection and diagnosis methods in wind turbine systems: A review
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of the fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) techniques that exist for wind turbine systems, which are classified into three categories: model-based methods, signal-based methods, and knowledge-based methods. The analysis of the reviewed papers shows that the performance of the diagnosis process is the highest in the case of advanced AI models, especially deep learning hybrid models. CNN-LSTM with attention mechanism achieves an accuracy of 95% for converter fault detection, one-dimensional CNN based on acoustic vibrations achieves an accuracy of 96.8%, Bayesian-GAN-LSTM achieves an accuracy of 97.6% for bearing fault diagnosis, and Graph LSTM achieves an accuracy of 95.2% for multi-component fault diagnosis. The accuracy of the tree-based random forest models for gearbox temperature-based classification is 86% while the enhanced random forest models on SCADA derived features is 99.72%. The multi-scale dense fusion networks and synchronized wavelet transform-CNN models achieve gearbox fault and planetary gearbox fault accuracy larger than 98%. Even with these developments, there are some key challenges: the lack of standardized benchmarking procedures, low model generalizability across a range of operating conditions, and computational limitations in real-time applications. The findings have led to this review concluding that data-driven and hybrid approaches are the most promising diagnostic capabilities that may be integrated into wind turbine condition monitoring systems, and that future research directions to make these systems more robust, more interpretable, and more deployable in practice include physics-informed learning, federated learning architectures, multi-modal data fusion, and explainable AI systems.

papers.title: FedPivot: Bridging Heterogeneous Multimodal Pre-training via Federated Post-Alignment
papers.abstract: The rapid evolution of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) is bottlenecked by the saturation of high-quality public data, while vast amounts of heterogeneous multimodal data remain inaccessible in privacy-sensitive silos. Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising solution to leverage these distributed resources while preserving privacy, but existing research focuses predominantly on fine-tuning, leaving the foundational pre-training phase largely unexplored. We argue that the core of MLLM pre-training lies in establishing effective cross-modal alignment, which bridges visual and textual representations into a unified semantic space. Motivated by this insight, we formally introduce the Federated Post-Alignment (Fed-PA) task, which studies cross-modal alignment under federated MLLM pre-training by collaboratively training a shared cross-modal projector. We identify two critical challenges in this setting: (i) parameter interference in aggregating local projectors; and (ii) gradient oscillations in one-pass collaborative SGD. To address these challenges, we propose FedPivot , a pioneering framework for federated post-alignment. FedPivot employs Canonical Reliability-Aware Aggregation (CRA) , which constructs a canonical space to decompose client projectors into a shared alignment basis and client-specific coefficients, then performs reliability-weighted fusion to suppress parameter interference. Furthermore, FedPivot introduces Orthogonality-Preserved Momentum (OPM) , which applies momentum to the shared alignment basis via orthogonal projection, accumulating historical optimization directions while preserving geometric structure. We construct four federated multimodal pre-training scenarios based on public datasets, and extensive experiments validate that FedPivot significantly outperforms existing baselines.

papers.title: Collaborative Mechanism of Privacy Computing and Blockchain in Multi-Center Medical Data Sharing
papers.abstract: The fragmentation of sensitive medical data across institutions and stringent privacy regulations creates isolated data silos, hindering the development of robust AI-driven healthcare solutions. Existing approaches often lack sufficient trust mechanisms, comprehensive auditability, and dynamic access control for multi-center collaboration. Goal: This protocol aims to resolve the tension between collaborative utility and data sovereignty by integrating federated learning (FL) with blockchain technology, providing a secure, auditable, and scalable framework for medical data sharing. The framework employs a tripartite architecture: cryptographic FL with adaptive regularization and Paillier homomorphic encryption for privacy-preserving local training; a multi-channel, tiered-sharding blockchain for decoupled access control, data provenance, and FL operation logging; and a dynamic privacy-computation coordination mechanism that adapts differential privacy and cryptographic protocols based on data sensitivity and hardware capability. The workflow follows a sequential set of steps, including data preprocessing, local encrypted gradient generation, blockchain-backed secure aggregation, and global model updating. Under experimental conditions, the framework achieved 92.5% model accuracy after 20 training rounds and supported up to 30 nodes. No raw data exposure was detected, and tamper detection succeeded in all evaluated test cases. The architecture reduced computational overhead by 41% compared to a centralized baseline, achieved 96% automated regulatory compliance for audited access approvals, and demonstrated linear scalability, with the block generation interval stabilizing at 4.2 s.
papers.venue: Journal of Visualized Experiments

papers.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning on Business Processes: A Socio-Technical Framework for Intelligent Process Automation, Decision Support, and Governance
authors: Laraib Tabish, Falak Ali, Maitikuerban Abuduaini
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) are moving from experimental projects into the operational core of organizations, where they increasingly execute, inform, and redesign business processes. Their effect is frequently described in terms of automation and efficiency, yet the actual consequences for a business process depend on where the technology is placed, how its outputs are routed into decisions, and whether the surrounding data, security, and governance arrangements can support it. This paper examines how modern AI, ML, and DL tools affect business processes across the full process lifecycle of design, execution, decisionmaking, monitoring, and improvement. Drawing on applied studies of ML-based face recognition, image-based electronic toll collection, peer-to-peer energy trading simulation, robotic process automation (RPA) and AI-bot identity management, low-code/no-code intelligent automation, real-time AI decision processing, human–bot discrimination, honeypot-based threat intelligence, and federated learning, the paper distinguishes three effects: task automation, decision augmentation, and process transformation. It then proposes a six-layer sociotechnical framework comprising process data and integration, AI/ML/DL intelligence, automation and execution, security, identity and privacy, governance and human oversight, and business value. A cost-sensitive, three-zone decision-routing model is introduced to show how confidence thresholds should be derived from business costs rather than from model accuracy alone, and a process-level evaluation framework is defined that combines quality, time, cost, risk, and human-oversight measures. The analysis concludes that AI improves business processes most reliably when it is applied to well-understood processes with standardized data, when automated decisions are bounded by explicit thresholds and human review, and when software bots are governed as accountable identities.

papers.title: FedGMix: code, configurations and results (v1.0.0)
papers.abstract: Code, configurations, pre-registration documents, per-run result files and analysis scripts for the article FedGMix: Stateless Federated Intrusion Detection with Shared Class-Conditional Mixtures under Label Skew and Site-Level Shift (A. Fahad, M. F. Alomari, Y. Aljeroudi). FedGMix is a stateless federated learning method for intrusion detection in which clients share global feature statistics and, once, a small Gaussian mixture per class; every client trains on its own flows plus balanced virtual samples drawn from the merged mixtures, and the server re-fits the classifier head only when federated validation improves. The archive also contains the site-shuffled test used to detect site-identity effects of client-local input normalisation. The datasets (CICIoT2023, Edge-IIoTset, TON_IoT) are public and are not redistributed; scripts/download_data.py fetches them. README.md maps configuration names to the method names used in the article.

papers.title: InstaFed: Instance-Aware Federated Learning with Noisy Labels
papers.abstract: Federated learning frequently encounters the challenge of label noise in real world scenarios. Existing robust methods commonly rely on local statistical partitioning to separate clean and noisy samples. However, this assumption breaks down under the sparse or heterogeneous local data common in federated settings. The resulting local statistical collapse destroys the bimodal loss structure, causing unreliable clean-noisy separation and optimization instability. To address this fundamental limitation, we propose InstaFed, a novel instance aware federated learning framework with formal theoretical guarantees for its core components. Instead of forcing scarce samples into unreliable statistical distributions, InstaFed tracks the longitudinal evolutionary trajectory of individual instances. This achieves highly precise noise decoupling that is independent of local data scale and class balance. Specifically, we utilize cumulative prediction entropy for privacy preserving client partitioning and maintain an exponential moving average of historical confidences to dynamically extract clean samples. Furthermore, we design a selective instance level semantic alignment mechanism that strictly neutralizes the memorization of corrupted labels without restricting the capacity of local models to learn authentic heterogeneous features. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that InstaFed significantly outperforms existing state of the art methods under various federated label noise settings.
papers.venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)

papers.title: Dual-Layer Defense: Blockchain-Secured Federated Learning Architecture for Trustworthy Anomaly Detection in IoT-Enabled Smart Grids
papers.abstract: Integrating the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) into smart grids improves their operational efficiency but expands their attack surface. Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative anomaly detection, but exchanged model updates remain exposed to tampering, impersonation, and replay. This paper proposes a dual-layer architecture in which FL performs distributed anomaly detection at edge nodes without sharing raw data, while a blockchain layer secures the exchanged parameters. Each local update is encrypted using ephemeral elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman key agreement, a hash-based message authentication code-based key-derivation function, and Advanced Encryption Standard in Galois/Counter Mode; committed through a Merkle root and a digital signature; and recorded by an Ethereum smart contract that enforces node registration and round consistency. Evaluated with nine non-independent and identically distributed clients on the UNSW-NB15 and Edge-IIoTset datasets, the architecture achieves accuracies of 81.41% and 94.76% and F1 scores of 85.55% and 94.81%, respectively. Because the parameters are recovered exactly, detection performance is unaffected. Securing one update requires 0.394 ms at the edge node and 0.518 ms at the global node for the UNSW-NB15, and 1.884 ms at the edge node and 2.229 ms at the global node for the Edge-IIoTset dataset. Functional security testing demonstrates that all tampering, replay, impersonation, and unauthorized-submission attempts were detected. Parameter-level integrity protection can therefore be added to FL-based anomaly detection at low cost.
papers.venue: Energies

papers.title: Federated Parameter-Efficient Selective Fine-Tuning for Vision-Language Models via Global-Local Masking
papers.abstract: While Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) with vision-language foundation models (VLMs) achieves strong in-domain performance in federated learning (FL), generalizing VLM-based FL methods to unseen domains remains challenging. To address this, this paper focuses on FL in base-to-new settings, examining two key trade-offs: (1) the performance trade-off between seen and unseen classes and (2) the performance trade-off among different clients. This paper explores selective mask-based PEFT, a technique rarely used for VLM-based FL, to address these two challenges, leveraging its ability to effectively utilize the prior knowledge of VLMs and its flexibility for client-specific adaptation. Specifically, we propose a personalized Federated Mask-based Selective PEFT framework (pFedMSF). To enhance generalization to unseen classes, pFedMSF employs binary masks to select a small subset of tunable weights, preserving the prior knowledge of the pre-trained VLM. To address the performance trade-off among clients, besides global masks shared by all clients, pFedMSF further introduces local mask for personalized model weight update to individual client. Experimental results show that pFedMSF significantly outperforms the existing federated PEFT method on both seen and unseen classes, and achieves balanced performance on all clients.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Intrusion and Anomaly Detection for Modern Cybersecurity
papers.abstract: Due to the increasing complexity of cyberattacks, old-school cybercrime detection methods are no longer effective. This chapter looks at how machine learning-based intrusion detection systems and anomaly detection solutions can revolutionise the way cybersecurity is done today. By using various different machine learning (ML) algorithms, such as supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning and find outliers (e.g. identify anomalies), detect new types of threats, and automatically respond to security incidents. This chapter provides a thorough overview of how ML is used for intrusion detection, including the use of deep learning algorithms for threat intelligence, behavioural and static analysis of malware, identifying phishing schemes using natural language processing, and detecting zero-day attacks. Additionally, this chapter dealing with unbalanced datasets, defending against adversarial attacks, using federated learning to cover multiple locations, and enabling explainability for ML-based cybersecurity.

papers.title: FLEET: Decentralized Execution Layer for Federated Learning and EV Energy Trading
papers.abstract: Integrating decentralized intelligence into peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading requires resilient, sustainable and accountable infrastructures for Electric Vehicle (EV) networks. Existing Blockchain-Federated Learning (FL) frameworks are constrained by on-chain data bottlenecks and computationally intensive cryptographic verifications. We propose FLEET, a 3-tier hierarchical framework decoupling edge AI from the blockchain and autonomously orchestrating energy trading, local model validation, and global intelligence distribution through smart contract governance and IPFS storage. Its key feature is Proof-of-Edge-Validation (PoEV), where Charging Stations execute FL while connected EVs act as auditors during charging, resolving the trade-off between energy-efficient networking and edge AI with lightweight validation. Combined with a reputation-weighted Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) overlay, FLEET reduces on-chain cost by up to 97.9% compared to cryptographic verification baselines and sustains 2,173 TPS as the network scales up to 102 stations, ensuring sustainable networking and accountable smart contract governance.

papers.title: FedHARDA: Federated Hard-Case Cascading Annotation without Raw Data Release
papers.abstract: In healthcare federated learning, clients often rely on lightweight local models for routine, low-cost inference, yet these models can become unreliable on challenging cases when incremental batches of unlabeled data arrive. External annotators could provide higher-quality labeling, but directly transmitting raw images for annotation is often undesirable and costly in practice. Motivated by this, we propose FedHARDA, a Federated Hard-case Cascading Annotation without Raw DAta Release framework that selectively invokes an external annotator while avoiding direct transmission of raw patient images. FedHARDA is built on two principles: efficient annotation of difficult cases and surrogate-based external supervision without direct transmission of raw images. Specifically, each client first identifies a minimal hard subset using a disagreement-aware selection strategy that combines divergence-consensus scoring with automated knee-point detection, thereby reducing unnecessary external queries. For each selected hard image, a locally deployed diffusion model generates multiple surrogate candidates. Only candidates that pass the PAC-calibrated retrieval-risk audit and semantic-fidelity filter are released to the external annotator. Returned external labels are used directly for surrogate supervision, without any voting or aggregation. Experiments across multiple medical image classification benchmarks show that FedHARDA consistently improves annotation accuracy while substantially reducing the number of external annotation queries.

papers.title: A federated learning-based globally coordinated cyber hygiene framework for individual users
papers.abstract: Cyber hygiene refers to the policies and practices governing the access, retrieval, and consumption of data and information by individual users, small and medium businesses, and large corporations. However, users, both individual and corporate, have been guilty of not practicing basic cyber hygiene, resulting in inadvertent financial losses, data theft, and security breaches. Thus, cyber hygiene enforcement is non-trivial, as poor cyber hygiene can potentially compromise even sophisticated security frameworks and tools. For a large number of individual users, the challenge is severely exacerbated, as they remain outside the scope of sophisticated security frameworks, making them susceptible to incidents of ransomware and other cyber attacks. Existing research has not adequately addressed the security concerns for individual users, focusing on simple tools, awareness, and advisories to address the security challenges. This research paper proposes a comprehensive cyber hygiene framework, focusing on real-time advisory for better cyber hygiene, combined with a globally coordinated federated learning framework for real-time threat detection and response formulation. The framework ensures that individual users stay protected from new emerging threats on a continuous basis. Experimental results establish the efficacy of the proposed framework.

papers.title: PrivFDM: Differentially Private Federated Diffusion Models for Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: Deploying Diffusion Models (DMs) in federated settings has recently attracted growing attention for their ability to harness the strong generative capacity of diffusion models. However, their practical deployment remains hindered by privacy risks, as sharing local models can potentially leak sensitive training data. To mitigate this, we propose PrivFDM, a differentially private federated diffusion model for image synthesis that generates high-fidelity synthetic images while ensuring rigorous privacy guarantees. PrivFDM presents a local pre-training method with autoencoder?based data perturbation that injects DP noise directly into the low?dimensional representations of the training data. This design reduces data sensitivity and significantly lowers privacy budget consumption. To support effective and private learning under heterogeneous client data, we further develop a local fine-tuning strategy with model perturbation and common knowledge sharing. By integrating DP?SGD and conditioning diffusion models through label embeddings, our approach mitigates the disruptive effect of client divergence and enhances the utility of the synthesized images. We theoretically prove that PrivFDM ensures DP guarantees across the entire federated training pipeline. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the strong performance and practical advantages of the proposed PrivFDM in federated learning.
papers.venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)

papers.title: FedFGS: Friend-Guided Synchronization and Geometric Stabilization for Federated Primal-Dual Learning under Sparse Participation
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative training without sharing raw data, but optimization becomes unstable under data heterogeneity and sparse participation. Federated primal-dual (FedPD) methods mitigate client drift by introducing dual variables to enforce consensus; however, under partial participation, inactive clients accumulate stale dual states, and their re-entry can induce severe primal-dual misalignment, degrading both convergence and generalization. To address this issue, we propose FedFGS, a FedPD framework that improves robustness under sparse participation through two complementary mechanisms. First, Friend-Guided Synchronization continuously evolves the reference dual states of inactive clients using cues from geometrically similar active clients, enabling a stable hot start upon re-entry. Second, Geometric Stabilization (GS) improves the reliability of friend estimation by stabilizing update geometry on the server side, preventing noisy similarity signals from corrupting synchronization. We further provide theoretical results on bounded virtual-dual deviation, GS perturbation stability, nonconvex stationarity, and generalization, where the effect of sparse-participation synchronization is explicitly characterized through a friend-mismatch term. Extensive experiments on standard federated benchmarks show that FedFGS consistently improves training stability, accelerates convergence, and enhances generalization, with especially pronounced gains under highly sparse participation.
papers.venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)

papers.title: Machine Learning Driven Analysis and Prediction of Hazardous Gas Concentrations: A Comprehensive Review of Sensing Data, Algorithms, and Emerging Applications
papers.abstract: Hazardous gases-carbon monoxide, hydrogen sulphide, ammonia, nitrogen oxides, methane, and volatile organic compounds-pose severe risks to health, industrial safety, and environmental quality, making continuous monitoring and early prediction a critical engineering priority.Conventional sensing systems, based on metal-oxidesemiconductor (MOS), electrochemical, and infrared transducers, suffer from crosssensitivity, baseline drift, and non-linear response, limiting the reliability of threshold-based alarms.Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have emerged as powerful tools for extracting selective, drift-resilient, and temporally predictive information from sensor signals, enabling accurate gas identification and multi-step-ahead concentration forecasting.This review surveys thirty recent studies (2020-2026) coupling hazardous gas sensing hardware with ML pipelines across domains including IoT-based indoor and rural air quality monitoring, underground coal mine safety, electronic nose (eNose) gas mixture identification, power transformer dissolved gas analysis, industrial emission control, and cyber-physical anomaly detection.Methodologies include classical algorithms (SVM, Random Forests, k-NN), ensembles (XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, Stacking), neural networks, and sequence-to-sequence models (LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, BiGRU, Transformer, Autoformer).The comparison proves that hybrid and bidirectional architectures deliver better performance in multi-step forecasting tasks compared to a single model, while tree-based ensembles continue to be relevant for low-latency edge computation tasks.The review highlights the difficulties connected with sensor drifting, dataset limitations, cross-sensitivity, and the challenge of transferring models from simulated environment to the real world, suggesting future research directions in federated learning, benchmarks, explainable AI, and edge-AI compression.

papers.title: Reported enterprise deployment readiness of privacy-preserving artificial intelligence: a governance and information management perspective
papers.abstract: Purpose Privacy-preserving artificial intelligence (AI) technologies increasingly support data-driven decision-making while safeguarding sensitive information. However, peer-reviewed evidence documenting governance integration and operational deployment remains limited. This study examines how the peer-reviewed academic literature documents the technical maturity, governance integration, and operational implementation of privacy-preserving AI systems relevant to enterprise information systems. Design/methodology/approach A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020-compliant systematic literature review examined 22 peer-reviewed studies published from 2018 to May 2026. The review synthesized evidence on privacy–utility trade-offs, governance integration, fairness, operational readiness, and implementation maturity. We used Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) and a proposed Translational Readiness Index (TRI) to classify readiness evidence reported in the included studies. Findings Privacy-preserving AI systems demonstrated favorable privacy–utility trade-offs in the reviewed academic literature, with privacy budgets of e = 1–3 preserving approximately 85–96% of baseline predictive performance. Federated learning combined with differential privacy was the dominant implementation architecture. Most included studies demonstrated intermediate technical maturity (TRL 4–6), primarily through controlled evaluations and prototype development while none documented deployment within operational payer workflows. Studies also inconsistently documented governance integration, privacy accounting, interoperability, and fairness assessment. We characterize this imbalance in the published academic evidence as the proposed Enterprise AI Documentation Gap Hypothesis. The hypothesis concerns the distribution of evidence in peer-reviewed literature and should not be interpreted as evidence that healthcare organizations or insurers are unprepared for deployment. Research limitations/implications This study is limited to reviewing scholarly papers published in the academic literature and did not systematically examine industry literature, company records, patent information, or practitioner views. Therefore, the results reflect the scholarly evidence base and do not reflect health organizations' or insurers' readiness for implementation. The absence of evidence in the literature on deployment does not imply that implementation does not occur outside scholarly journals. Future studies should cross-check scholarly evidence with industry and practitioner evidence on the same topic. Originality/value The TRI offers an exploratory, multidimensional framework for organizing documented evidence across technology, privacy, governance, fairness, and operations. This study proposes the Enterprise AI Documentation Gap Hypothesis to describe the gap between the relative maturity of technical evidence and the lack of published evidence on governance and operations. These are conceptual contributions that require further empirical testing.
papers.venue: Journal of Enterprise Information Management

papers.title: Anomaly Detection and Cyber Attack Mitigation Using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of digital infrastructure has made cyber threats more complex and widespread, requiring more advanced, flexible security systems. This chapter provides a study on how machine learning can help find strange behavior and stop cyberattacks, with a focus on the move from signature-based systems to behaviour-driven ones. It explains supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, and reinforcement learning methods for detecting both known and unknown threats. The study identifies significant challenges, including class imbalance, false positives, adversarial attacks, and data privacy issues. The chapter shows how intelligent, adaptable, and scalable machine learning models improve cybersecurity resilience and make it possible to use proactive defense strategies in changing environments by using real-world case studies and modern frameworks like federated learning and explainable AI.
papers.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series

papers.title: Federated meta-learning with gradient-parameter aggregation for load forecasting under data scarcity
papers.abstract: Short-term load forecasting is critical for grid stability and energy management, yet growing privacy concerns and data ownership regulations increasingly restrict the centralized data aggregation that current methods rely on. Federated learning enables model training without raw data sharing, but existing federated forecasting methods assume sufficient local data at each client, an assumption that does not hold for all individual residential consumers. To address the need for distributed learning with limited data, this paper presents FedGPA ( Fed erated Meta-Learning via G radient- P arameter A ggregation), which trains a single global model under federated few-shot conditions using both gradient-based and parameter-based knowledge. FedGPA introduces a two-stage knowledge aggregation procedure, Multi-Perspective Weighted Aggregation, and Gradient-Parameter Fusion to balance fast adaptation with global stability across distributed, data-scarce nodes. Specifically, MPWA balances uniform, loss-weighted, and distance-weighted aggregation signals to improve global model consistency, while GPF adaptively combines gradient and parameter knowledge to enable stable convergence under data scarcity. Experiments on real-world residential households compare FedGPA against centralized and federated baselines using LSTM and Transformer architectures across varying forecasting horizons. FedGPA consistently outperforms all baselines across configurations while preserving data privacy.

papers.title: CIFL: Byzantine Attacks and Robustness in Federated Learning with Class-Isolated Clients

papers.title: Privacy-preserving federated learning with differential privacy for secure distributed intelligent computing
papers.abstract: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralized data sharing, making it suitable for privacy-sensitive intelligent computing environments. However, FL models remain vulnerable to information leakage through model updates and prediction outputs, particularly when learning from electroencephalography (EEG) signals. Although Differential Privacy (DP) can mitigate such risks, integrating DP into distributed deep learning often reduces predictive performance and destabilizes optimization. To address these challenges, this study proposes SAFE (Secure Adaptive Federated EEG Framework), a privacy-preserving distributed learning framework integrating representation-level DP, TLS-secured communication, and multi-round Federated Averaging (FedAvg) optimization. SAFE applies Laplace-based DP directly to normalized EEG representations prior to local training while preserving decentralized data locality. The framework was evaluated using EEGNet, ShallowNet, and EEGTCNet on the BCI Competition IV Dataset 2a under multiple privacy budgets ( $$\epsilon = 1, 5, 10$$ ) across 20 communication rounds. Experimental evaluation using classification accuracy, convergence analysis, communication overhead, and Membership Inference Attacks (MIA) demonstrated that SAFE effectively balanced predictive utility and privacy protection. Among the evaluated models, ShallowNet achieved the strongest federated performance and convergence stability. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of integrating DP and secure communication into federated EEG learning without substantial degradation in predictive utility.
papers.venue: Discover Computing

papers.title: Secure Enterprise Data Fabric using Federated Learning and Sovereign Cloud Architecture for Privacy Engineering
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and distributed data ecosystems has created significant opportunities for enterprises while simultaneously intensifying concerns surrounding data privacy, sovereignty, security, and regulatory compliance. This paper proposes a secure enterprise data fabric that integrates federated learning with sovereign cloud architecture to establish a privacy-oriented framework for distributed enterprise data management and analytics. The proposed approach enables organizations to retain sensitive datasets within jurisdictionally controlled environments while allowing machine-learning models to learn collaboratively without requiring raw data to be centrally transferred. Sovereign cloud principles are incorporated through jurisdiction-aware data residency, controlled infrastructure ownership, identity governance, encryption, auditability, and policy-based access mechanisms. Federated learning complements these controls by decentralizing model training and reducing unnecessary exposure of confidential information. The research methodology adopts a mixed conceptual and experimental approach involving architecture design, threat modeling, privacy assessment, security evaluation, and comparative performance analysis. Key evaluation dimensions include data exposure, privacy preservation, model utility, communication overhead, latency, compliance alignment, and resilience against adversarial attacks. The proposed data fabric is intended to provide enterprises with a scalable foundation for privacy engineering in multi-cloud and cross-organizational environments. The study demonstrates how federated intelligence and sovereign infrastructure can be integrated into a unified security architecture that balances analytical utility with organizational and regulatory requirements.
papers.venue: Journal of Cyber-Physical Security and Robotics

papers.title: HYBRID FEDERATED LEARNING ARCHITECTURE FOR PRIVACY-PRESERVING AI IN GREEN HYDROGEN ENERGY SYSTEMS: A REVIEW
papers.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, and smart grids into green hydrogen energy systems creates opportunities for improved energy forecasting, electrolyzer optimization, predictive maintenance, and operational efficiency. However, the interconnected nature of these infrastructures introduces significant challenges relating to data privacy, cybersecurity, commercial confidentiality, and organizational compliance. This review examines the potential of a hybrid federated learning architecture for privacy-preserving AI in green hydrogen energy systems. Drawing on literature concerning green hydrogen technologies, federated learning, differential privacy, blockchain-enabled security, Privacy Calculus Theory, and the Selective Organizational Information Privacy and Security Violations Model (SOIPSV), the review synthesizes existing approaches and identifies unresolved technical and governance challenges. It conceptualizes a six-layer architecture comprising edge and local processing, privacy calculus, federated learning, secure aggregation, organizational governance, and global intelligence. The proposed architecture integrates privacy-risk and benefit assessment, decentralized model training, cryptographic protection, and policy-oriented accountability to support collaborative intelligence across distributed hydrogen production facilities and smart grid networks. The framework remains conceptual and has not undergone empirical validation, simulation benchmarking, or real-world deployment. Its predictive performance, computational overhead, privacy guarantees, and scalability remain unverified. The review identifies future research priorities, including formal privacy accounting, adversarial testing, standardized benchmarks, governance operationalization, and pilot implementation. This synthesis provides a foundation for developing and evaluating trustworthy, privacy-aware AI architectures for secure and sustainable green hydrogen infrastructure.
